t1_email.subject: Your last report is one click away
t1_email.preheader: Rerun it with this week's numbers
t1_email.headline: Pick up where your report left off
paragraphs: Hi {first_name}, the last time you were in {product_name} you built a report from your connected data. It is still there, and it will rerun with this week's numbers the moment you open it.
Most weekly reports take a minute once the data source is connected, and yours already is.
If something got in the way, reply to this email and tell me what. I read every reply.
t1_email.hypothesis: Pointing to the report they already built lowers the effort of coming back; falsified if B's fresh-start framing recovers as many or more users within 7 days.

t1_email.subject: This week's numbers are ready to pull
t1_email.preheader: Your data sources are still connected
t1_email.headline: Your data kept arriving while you were away
paragraphs: Hi {first_name}, your data sources in {product_name} have kept syncing, so a report built today would show the last two weeks you have not looked at yet.
Start from a blank report or from one of the templates on the reports page. Either way the numbers fill in on their own.
If a report is not what you need right now, reply and tell me what would be.
t1_email.hypothesis: Framing the gap as unseen data creates a reason to return now; falsified if A recovers as many or more users within 7 days.

t2_email.subject: The two-minute way to build a report
t2_email.preheader: Start from a template instead of a blank page
t2_email.headline: Skip the blank page
paragraphs: Hi {first_name}, the most common reason people stop after onboarding is the blank report page: it is not obvious what to put on it first.
The report templates in {product_name} start you with the charts most teams build first. Pick one, point it at a connected data source, and change what you like.
It takes about two minutes, and you can delete it if it is not useful.
t2_email.hypothesis: Naming the blank-page problem and handing over a template removes the main friction; falsified if B's offer of a person recovers as many or more users.

t2_email.subject: Want me to build your first report?
t2_email.preheader: Reply with what you track and I will set it up
t2_email.headline: Tell me what you track
paragraphs: Hi {first_name}, setting up the first report is where a lot of people get stuck, usually because it is not clear which numbers belong on it.
Reply to this email with the two or three numbers you check every week, and I will set up a report in your {product_name} account that shows them.
No call needed. You will get an email when it is ready.
t2_email.hypothesis: Offering a person removes the friction for people who are unsure what to build; falsified if A's template path recovers as many or more users.

t3_in_app.headline: New: start a report from a template
t3_in_app.body: Report templates start you with the charts most teams build first. Pick one and point it at a connected data source.
t3_in_app.hypothesis: Showing templates at the next session converts users who returned on their own but did not build; falsified if B recovers as many or more.

t3_in_app.headline: Your data sources are still syncing
t3_in_app.body: A report built now would show everything that arrived while you were away. Start one in under two minutes.
t3_in_app.hypothesis: The unseen-data framing works better in product than the feature framing; falsified if A recovers as many or more.

t4_email.subject: How our support team builds its weekly report
t4_email.preheader: Five minutes on Monday, then it runs itself
t4_email.headline: One report, five minutes, every Monday
paragraphs: Hi {first_name}, our own support team uses {product_name} for a weekly report of open tickets, response times and the busiest hours. Here is exactly how they set it up.
They started from the support template, connected the help desk as a data source, and scheduled the report to land in the team channel every Monday morning.
The setup took about five minutes, and nobody has touched it since. The same steps work for any weekly number you track.
t4_email.hypothesis: A concrete first-party example makes the weekly habit easy to copy; falsified if B's scheduling angle recovers as many or more users.

t4_email.subject: Have your report come to you
t4_email.preheader: Schedule it once and it lands every Monday
t4_email.headline: Reports you do not have to remember
paragraphs: Hi {first_name}, here is how our own support team keeps up with its numbers without logging in: a {product_name} report scheduled to arrive in the team channel every Monday.
Build any report, choose a schedule and where it should go, and it shows up on its own after that.
If you only want one number a week, that is a fine report too.
t4_email.hypothesis: Scheduling answers the forgetting that causes the lapse; falsified if A recovers as many or more users.

t5_email.subject: Should I keep sending these?
t5_email.preheader: One click to stay, or do nothing to stop
t5_email.headline: Do you still want these emails?
paragraphs: Hi {first_name}, I have sent a few notes about {product_name} reports and I do not want to fill your inbox with ones you do not read.
If you would like to keep hearing from us, click below. If you do nothing, I will stop sending these product emails. Your account and your reports stay exactly as they are.
t5_email.hypothesis: A plain question with a clear default keeps engaged people and quietly removes the rest; falsified if B's version keeps a larger share of clickers with no rise in complaints.

t5_email.subject: Last note from me about reports
t5_email.preheader: Click if you want more, otherwise I will stop
t5_email.headline: Keep hearing from us?
paragraphs: Hi {first_name}, this is the last email in this series. If you want tips on getting more out of {product_name}, click below and I will keep you on the list.
If not, you do not need to do anything. These emails stop, and nothing in your account changes.
t5_email.hypothesis: Marking this as the last note raises the stay rate among people who still care; falsified if A keeps as many or more clickers.
